title: A Ledger for the Portrait
premise: When the coffin of Ashford Bell, founder of the river town of Marrow's Bend, is exhumed for a land dispute, it proves empty — and insurance investigator Hazel Delacroix, whose photographic memory makes them both invaluable and haunted, is hired by the estate to find out why. Digging through thirty-year-old ledgers, portraits, and alibis, Hazel discovers that Bell faked his death to escape a fraud trial, that several of the town's founding families helped bury the secret, and that the town's beloved matriarch, Odette Marsh, has been signing letters in Bell's hand ever since. The killer of the one witness who tried to speak — Hazel's estranged foster brother, Theo — turns out to be Odette's son, who killed to protect the lie that gave him his inheritance and his name. In the end, Hazel chooses truth over belonging: they testify at trial, the town fractures but survives, and Hazel finally claims a found family built on honesty rather than shared silence.
about_author: Petra Voss is a former forensic archivist who spent a decade cataloguing cold-case evidence before turning to fiction full-time. She writes mysteries about memory and small-town complicity from a converted boathouse on the Hudson.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Oak
chapters.summary: Hazel Delacroix, POV. At the exhumation ordered for a land-title dispute, Hazel watches the coffin of town founder Ashford Bell come up light — and empty. The crowd's gasp, the gravedigger's pale face, everything photographs itself into Hazel's memory unbidden. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into professional hunger as Hazel realizes this case will not stay buried.

chapters.title: Retained by the Dead
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. The Bell estate's lawyer, Corinne Ashe, hires Hazel to investigate quietly before the fraud-trial reopening forces the issue. Hazel reviews the 1994 death certificate, funeral photos, and the famous portrait of Bell that hangs in the town hall. Beat: controlled competence masking the first flicker of recognition — Hazel knew someone at that funeral.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Hazel interviews the old guard: Mayor Pruett, undertaker Silas Crane, and matriarch Odette Marsh, each offering polished, suspiciously identical accounts of Bell's final days. Their stories align too perfectly, like rehearsed testimony. Beat: growing certainty that Marrow's Bend agreed on its history long ago and intends to keep it.

chapters.title: The Boy in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Sorting funeral photos, Hazel's photographic memory snags on a teenage boy at the graveside — Theo, their estranged foster brother, now the town archivist. Their reunion is brittle, full of old wounds. Beat: bittersweet longing; Hazel wants reconnection but suspects Theo knows more than he says.

chapters.title: Ledger Entries in Red Ink
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. In the archive cellar, Theo finds Bell's business ledger with entries in red ink that don't match any known account — payments continuing after the death date. He hides the page from Hazel, torn between loyalty to the town that took him in and loyalty to the sibling he abandoned. Beat: guilt curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Portrait of a Liar
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. An art restorer reveals the town-hall portrait was painted over an earlier canvas — dated two years after Bell's supposed death. Someone commissioned a portrait of a dead man while he lived. Beat: exhilaration of the breakthrough shadowed by dread; the conspiracy has money and patience.

chapters.title: What Odette Keeps in the Attic
chapters.summary: Odette, POV. Odette Marsh rereads decades of letters written in her own hand but signed 'A. Bell,' which she has sent to herself to keep the fiction alive. She loves the town like a child and will not let it be orphaned by truth. Beat: chilling tenderness — the antagonist's motive revealed as devotion.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wouldn't Stay Buried
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. A retired bank clerk, Marguerite Doyle, contacts Hazel claiming she processed Bell's withdrawals in 1996 — two years post-mortem. Before Hazel can reach her, Marguerite's house burns with her inside. Beat: horror and self-reproach; Hazel's investigation may have painted a target.

chapters.title: Ash and Accelerant
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Examining fire-scene photos, Hazel's memory isolates a detail everyone missed: a second set of footprints in the flowerbed ash, size twelve, retreating. Sheriff Ives dismisses it as accident. Beat: isolation deepens; Hazel realizes the law itself may be part of the town's pact of silence.

chapters.title: Foster Care, Foster Lies
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Flashback chapter: Theo and Hazel's childhood in the Delacroix foster home, the promise they made never to abandon each other, and the night Theo chose the Marsh family's adoption over staying with Hazel. Beat: heartbreak explaining the present rift and why Theo owes Odette everything — and hates it.

chapters.title: The Second Coffin
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Following land records, Hazel finds a private burial plot on Marsh property holding an unmarked grave — and soil tests suggest a body interred around 1994. Whose? Beat: grim momentum; the mystery shifts from where Bell went to who else died keeping his secret.

chapters.title: Silas Sings
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Confronted with the plot, the aging undertaker Silas Crane breaks: Bell didn't die; Bell's bookkeeper did, in a panic gone wrong, and they buried the bookkeeper in Bell's place. Silas names no one else but begs Hazel to stop before more old people die. Beat: pity and fury entwined; the first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Letters to Myself
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Hazel obtains Odette's mail pattern through the postal inquiry and realizes the 'Bell correspondence' sustaining his legend flows from Odette's own house. Confronting her, Hazel meets serene denial and a veiled threat about Hazel's standing in town. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Hazel understands Odette is the spider.

chapters.title: The Son Who Inherited a Ghost
chapters.summary: Emmett Marsh, POV. Odette's son Emmett, who inherited Bell's fortune through a trust contingent on Bell's 'death,' cleans his father's old rifle and rereads Marguerite's threatening letter. He believes he protects his mother and his name. Beat: cold dread; the reader sees the killer's logic before Hazel does.

chapters.title: Photographic Evidence
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Hazel reconstructs the funeral from memory, placing every attendee, and realizes Emmett claimed to be in Chicago during the week the bookkeeper vanished — yet appears, out of focus, in Hazel's own recollection of the marina. Beat: triumph of the gift; the alibi begins to rot under scrutiny.

chapters.title: Theo's Choice
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Emmett, sensing exposure, offers Theo the archivist position for life if he loses one ledger page. Theo photographs every page instead and sends copies to Hazel, then disappears. Beat: redemption in motion; the siblings' broken promise finally honored, at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Missing
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Theo vanishes; his apartment is searched, his car found at the marina. Hazel, terrified the past is repeating, uses every favor and every memory trick to trace him, finding a hidden cabin key taped beneath a drawer in the archive. Beat: raw fear transmuted into ferocious resolve — Hazel will not lose him twice.

chapters.title: The Cabin at Bellwater
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. At the cabin, Hazel finds Theo alive but cornered, and Emmett arriving with the rifle. A standoff in the dark: Emmett confesses to killing Marguerite and, thirty years ago, the bookkeeper — a panicked shove that became a life of lies. Beat: climax of danger; Hazel talks, records, and stalls until Sheriff Ives, finally choosing courage, arrives.

chapters.title: Arrest at the Portrait's Feet
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Emmett is arrested in the town hall beneath Bell's overpainted portrait as the whole town watches. Odette publicly takes responsibility for the letters, shattering the founding families' united front. Beat: cathartic public reckoning; the beautiful lie collapses in the most symbolic room in town.

chapters.title: Preparation for Trial
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. As prosecutor, Hazel organizes three decades of evidence — ledgers, soil samples, the recording — knowing the defense will attack their memory as unreliable narration. Theo testifies about the ledger despite threats. Beat: anxious diligence; justice approaches but nothing feels guaranteed.

chapters.title: The Verdict
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, brief rotating sections. The jury convicts Emmett of murder; Odette receives probation and public shame; the town argues in diners and churchyards about whether truth was worth the wound. Beat: bittersweet vindication — victory that costs the community its innocence.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV. Months later, Hazel and Theo open a small investigative office together above the restored archive, and the town plants a tree where the empty coffin lay. Hazel writes the case's final page in a new ledger — one meant to be read. Beat: quiet hope; identity and family rebuilt on truth instead of silence.
